title: OneDrive and SharePoint: annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs in the web viewer
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes Microsoft's planned protected-PDF annotation capability from existing sensitivity-label controls. The corrected explanation of permission changes matches Learn; the only finding is that the label-management UI path stops at the label list rather than the permission settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Purview route Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling enables PDF support when the banner is present.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... Then, if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner to confirm you want to turn on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true enables the existing PDF sensitivity-label support setting in SharePoint Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF ... Allows tenant admins to turn on support for PDFs with sensitivity labels ... True - Enables support for PDFs.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].scope; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing PDF support control operates at tenant scope for sensitivity labels on PDFs in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Allows tenant admins to turn on support for PDFs with sensitivity labels for the following scenarios: ... Auto-labeling policies and default sensitivity labels for SharePoint document libraries.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Running Set-SPOTenant requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels in the Microsoft Purview portal is the route shown for managing a label's encryption permissions.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching rendered path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now > Assign permissions > Choose permissions'. Set controls[1].ui.docs and its rendered Learn link to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels, which documents the permission settings. Retain create-sensitivity-labels in sources for the route to editing a label.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-Label with Identity and EncryptionRightsDefinitions modifies the usage rights assigned by an existing label's encryption configuration.
claims.quote: Use the Set-Label cmdlet to modify sensitivity labels in your organization. ... The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected. ... The Identity parameter specifies the sensitivity label that you want to modify.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A label's encryption settings are on its Access control page, including Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose one of the following options: ... Assign permissions now

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, administrators must connect to each geo-location and enable PDF support separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo: Similarly to the instructions to run the PowerShell command to enable support for sensitivity labels, you must connect to each of your geo-locations, and then run the command to enable support for PDFs.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: For items already encrypted using Assign permissions now, changed users or permissions apply to existing items when users authenticate with the encryption service.
claims.quote: For items that are already labeled with encryption and the assign permissions now option, when you change the encryption settings for users or permissions, the new settings will be applied for existing items when users authenticate with the encryption service.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Users who already opened the encrypted item receive changed settings after their existing use licence expires and they reauthenticate.
claims.quote: However, if users have already opened an encrypted document or email, they won't get the new settings until their use license has expired and they must reauthenticate.
